a.xlink:title:
Stub for METIS-2594: METIS internal calibration shall provide a range of flux levels matching that encountered in scientific operation as defined in METIS-3137.
Writes nothing (the scenario's cases are still checked, so the config stays valid for a future implementation).
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files (empty)
a.text: a range of flux levels matching

a.xlink:title:
Simulated data for METIS-2883: the source used for detector linearity calibration shall provide an illumination that is spatially homogeneous within +/- 3% peak-to-valley over the science field of view.
Per case, a full-aperture ScopeSim flat with a smooth illumination pattern injected so that max |pixel / mean - 1| = injected half_ptv (on top of whatever inhomogeneity ScopeSim itself produces). Writes one PASS case and one FAIL case (and e.g. one near the limit, if configured).
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files

Simulated data for METIS-3300: the level of flux of the flat field shall be tunable to 15 discrete values and shall be known at each step to 0.3%; the resulting spatial illumination pattern shall remain constant across the field within 0.5% after tuning.
Flux steps: the WCU black-body aperture is fixed (bb_aperture); the exposure E = T_ND x DIT is stepped linearly, E_k = E_max * k / n_steps (header NOMFLUX = k / n_steps, the nominal relative flux). E_max puts the raw peak (background included, which scales with E too) at sim_common.MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation / (1 + peak_margin), scaled from the probe ctx.lit_frame() (base ND and DIT). Per step, the least attenuating ND of nd_filters with DIT = E_k / T_ND >= the detector's minimum DIT is used (choose_nd_and_dit), with two darks and a flat read out at that ND and DIT (the background scales with it). Per case and step, injected: - flux error: the flux is off the nominal by +/- flux_error (alternating sign), - pattern change: a smooth pattern with amplitude ramping from -pattern_change to +pattern_change over the steps (so each step's normalised flat differs from the step-averaged one by at most pattern_change). Writes ..._<case>_stepNN.fits for one PASS case and one FAIL case (more if configured), one ScopeSim readout per step shared by all cases.
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files
a.text: level of flux of the flat field

a.xlink:title:
Simulated data for METIS-3291: METIS shall allow the characterisation and correction of the relative spectral response function (RSRF) with 3% precision over the wavelength range specified in METIS-1090.
WORK IN PROGRESS: the body is still a copy of simulate_metis_3300 (flat-field flux steps), not an RSRF simulation. As it stands it needs the METIS-3300 keys in the scenario entry (n_steps, bb_aperture, nd_filters, peak_margin, and both flux_error and pattern_change in each case's inject), and does the following.
Flux steps: the WCU black-body aperture is fixed (bb_aperture); the exposure E = T_ND x DIT is stepped linearly, E_k = E_max * k / n_steps (header NOMFLUX = k / n_steps, the nominal relative flux). E_max puts the raw peak (background included, which scales with E too) at sim_common.MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation / (1 + peak_margin), scaled from a probe flat (base ND and DIT). Per step, the least attenuating ND of nd_filters with DIT = E_k / T_ND >= the detector's minimum DIT is used (choose_nd_and_dit), with two darks and a flat read out at that ND and DIT (the background scales with it). Per case and step, injected: - flux error: the flux is off the nominal by +/- flux_error (alternating sign), - pattern change: a smooth pattern with amplitude ramping from -pattern_change to +pattern_change over the steps (so each step's normalised flat differs from the step-averaged one by at most pattern_change). Writes ..._<case>_stepNN.fits for each configured case, one ScopeSim readout per step shared by all cases.
OUTPUTS: - list[str]: written files

a.xlink:title:
Run the requirement simulators of a scenario config: for each instrument, one OpticalTrain, with the DIT shortened if needed so the raw readout (aperture fully open) peaks at <= MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation (limit_dit_to_saturation); for each requirement with simulate: true that applies to it, the requirement's simulator, simulator(ctx, req_key, req_cfg) -> list of written files, with req_cfg resolved for the instrument's detector (see resolve_for_detector).
INPUTS: - scenario (dict): the scenario config - simulators (dict): requirement key -> simulator function - observing (dict): merged observing config (common + test-specific) - out_dir (str): directory to write to - test_prefix (str): file name prefix, e.g. 'IMG_OPT_04' - results_dir (str or None): directory for FYI plots (ctx.results_dir), if any
OUTPUTS: - dict: (requirement key, instrument name) -> list of written files

Load the common observing config, then merge each test-specific config on top, in order (top-level keys of later files override earlier ones).
INPUTS ---------- stem : str Project root (METIS_MAIT_code_eckhart/), prepended to relative paths. *test_config_files : str Test-specific observing configs, relative to stem or absolute.
OUTPUTS ------- dict The merged observing config.

Load a YAML configuration file and pipe its contents to the log.
INPUTS ---------- config_file_choice : str Path to the configuration file. print_one_line : bool, optional If True, log the entire config on a single line. If False (default), log in a more readable, multiline format.
OUTPUTS ------- config_this : dict The configuration dictionary loaded from file.

a.xlink:title: Observe with the WCU black-body aperture at bb_aperture and read out one frame.
Put ND filter `filter` (one of the ND wheel's, e.g. 'ND_OD3') in the beam.
Two independent darks (black-body aperture closed): dark_1 to extract the signal from the illuminated frames, dark_2 to write out as BACKGROUND.

Write one case: primary header (ScopeSim's + set-up + requirement cards), then BCKGD_SUBTED (raw - background), RAW_READOUT and BACKGROUND, as float32, then extra_hdus (astropy HDUs, written as given). If saturation_adu is given, the header also gets SAT_ADU and PEAKFRAC (max of the raw readout / saturation), and a warning is logged if PEAKFRAC > MAX_RAW_FRAC.
OUTPUTS: - str: path of the written file

a.xlink:title: Saturation level (ADU per DIT) of a detector from the observing config, or None.
Detector key ('img_lm' or 'img_n') of a WCU imaging obs_mode.

Shorten the DIT, if needed, so that the peak of the raw readout (aperture fully open) is <= max_frac * saturation_adu. Never lengthens it.
Each trial takes a dark and an illuminated readout at the current DIT. If the raw peak is too high, the DIT is rescaled to aim at target_frac * saturation, assuming the signal is linear in DIT on top of the dark level: dit_new = dit * (target_frac * sat - median(dark)) / (peak - median(dark)), at most halving the DIT per trial if the peak is at saturation (the readout may be clipped there, which makes the linear estimate too optimistic). The readouts are per DIT (ScopeSim averages over NDIT), so NDIT is left as it is; the trials use trial_ndit (default 1: quick, and the noisier peak errs on the safe side; None for the configured NDIT).
INPUTS: - metis: OpticalTrain - instrument (dict): instrument config, with 'dit' and 'ndit' (not modified) - saturation_adu (float): saturation level (ADU per DIT) - max_frac, target_frac (float): limit and aim for the raw peak, as fractions of saturation - max_iter (int): maximum number of trials - readout_fn: readout function, readout_fn(metis, bb_aperture, instrument) -> (frame, header); injectable for tests - trial_ndit (int or None): NDIT of the trial readouts
OUTPUTS: - dict: a copy of instrument with 'dit' set to the tuned DIT - dict: dit_cfg, dit, peak_frac (raw peak / saturation of the last trial), n_trials
Raises ValueError if the dark level alone is >= target_frac * saturation, and RuntimeError if no DIT within max_iter trials is short enough.

that the peak of the raw readout
